Extra Gooey Cinnamon Rolls (Bakery-Style & No-Knead) Dough * 1 tsp yeast * 2 tbsp sugar * 343 g milk (about 1½ cups) * 480 g flour (about 4 cups + 2 tbsp) * 1 tsp salt * 60 g softened butter (about 4 tbsp) Filling * 140 g softened butter (10 tbsp) * 140 g brown sugar (about ⅔ cup) * 3½ tbsp ground cinnamon Butter Vanilla Frosting * 85 g softened butter (6 tbsp) * 180 g powdered sugar (about 1½ cups) * 1 tbsp vanilla extract Instructions 1. In a bowl, mix the yeast, sugar, and milk. Add the flour and mix until combined. Add the salt and softened butter, then stretch and fold (or coil fold) until the butter is fully incorporated. 2. Cover and let the dough rise for about 2 hours, or until doubled in size. 3. Roll the dough into a large rectangle. Spread the softened butter evenly over the dough, then sprinkle with the brown sugar and cinnamon. 4. Cut the dough into 6 long strips, then roll each strip into a cinnamon roll. 5. Sprinkle a little of the cinnamon sugar mixture into the bottom of the pan, then place the rolls on top. 6. Cover and let them rest for 15 minutes. 7. Mix a little milk with 1 tbsp melted butter, then spoon about 2 tbsp of the mixture over each cinnamon roll. 8. Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 25–30 minutes, or until golden brown. 9. As soon as they come out of the oven, cover them with a clean kitchen towel until warm. Then spread the frosting on top. Veterinary professionals have one of the highest suicide rates of any profession. At the same time, many others are leaving veterinary medicine altogether. There isn’t one single reason why, but one thing I wish more people understood is the emotional toll of being told you’re “only in it for the money” or accused of trying to manipulate people simply because you ask for payment for medical care. Veterinary clinics are businesses with staff to pay, equipment to maintain, medications to stock, and hospitals to keep open. None of that changes when a patient is critically ill. Every veterinarian I know wishes every pet could receive every treatment they need regardless of cost, but wanting that and actually being able to provide it for free are two very different things. Before assuming the worst, remember that the person on the other side of the exam table has likely dedicated years of their life, accumulated significant educational debt, and carries the weight of difficult decisions every single day. A little empathy goes a long way, for everyone involved. #VeterinaryMedicine #VetMed #Veterinarian #MentalHealth #TheHonestVet
